meta.description: Turns an enrichResult or gseaResult from clusterProfiler/enrichplot into a figure that collapses or shows gene-set redundancy, using dotplot, barplot, cnetplot, emapplot, treeplot, ridgeplot, gseaplot2, and upsetplot. Covers why cnetplot/emapplot/treeplot need pairwise_termsim first, why enrichplot ships no barplot for gseaResult, why GeneRatio is not fold enrichment, and why showCategory silently truncates.

scientific_integrity.detail: All citations checked against real, correctly-attributed papers (Wu 2021 The Innovation, Yu 2010 Bioinformatics, Supek 2011 PLoS One, Merico 2010 PLoS One, Reimand 2019 Nat Protoc, Subramanian 2005 PNAS). No fabricated statistics; all numeric claims (GeneRatio formula, redundancy counts, NES signs) verified against live execution, not invented.

practice_boundaries.detail: Pure bioinformatics visualization of researcher-supplied gene-set objects; no patient data, no diagnostic or prescriptive content; medical disclaimer not applicable to this scope.

methodological_ground.detail: No methodological fallacy found across 5 executed inputs; the Skill's central claims (GeneRatio != fold enrichment, GSEA NES is signed and must not be barplotted, GO-DAG redundancy inflates naive top-N lists) were independently verified against real clusterProfiler/enrichplot output, not merely asserted.

code_usability.detail: Both shipped example scripts (visualization_ora.R, visualization_gsea.R) ran end-to-end with zero modification on real clusterProfiler/enrichplot/org.Hs.eg.db (exit 0, valid PDFs). All 5 constructed inputs executed; failures found (treeplot on compareClusterResult, upsetplot needing ggupset) are missing-dependency/API-churn issues, not syntax errors or unrunnable code -- see recommendations.

functional_suitability.note: Covers the full enrichplot surface (dotplot/barplot/cnetplot/emapplot/treeplot/ridgeplot/gseaplot2/upsetplot/goplot/heatplot) with a decision tree, object model, and quantitative thresholds. Correctness verified largely accurate by execution (GeneRatio formula, no-barplot-for-gseaResult, redundancy claim all confirmed); minor imprecision: treeplot is listed as 'ORA + GSEA' with no caveat that it crashes on compareClusterResult under the installed enrichplot/ggplot2 combination, and the primary example's own 'nCluster' argument is already flagged deprecated by the installed package.

reliability.note: Common Errors table (8 rows) and Per-Method Failure Modes section (6 entries) are specific and give a Fix for each. Two gaps found only by execution: upsetplot's ggupset dependency is entirely undocumented (ridgeplot/goplot's ggridges/ggarchery ARE documented), and treeplot-on-compareClusterResult's crash is not covered by the Version Compatibility note, which otherwise correctly anticipates cnetplot/emapplot/goplot argument churn.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md (~230 lines) is dense but entirely load-bearing for a plotting decision-support skill; example code and prompt catalogue are correctly offloaded to usage-guide.md and examples/, not inlined. Workflow itself (class -> redundancy decision -> termsim if needed -> plot -> save) is linear with no redundant round-trips.

agent_usability.note: Strong cold-start clarity (leads with the one modeling-choice insight the rest of the skill hangs off), consistent terminology throughout, explicit output/caption expectations (report total significant count, similarity method, min_edge), and two full sections (Per-Method Failure Modes, Common Errors) proactively warning against the exact mistakes execution testing reproduced.

human_usability.note: Frontmatter description is somewhat technical (leads with enrichResult/gseaResult/S4 class terms); usage-guide.md's Quick Start compensates with natural phrasing ('Make a dotplot of my GO enrichment...'). Category-3 Scene Override credited: the 'introspect and adapt rather than pin one API generation' instruction is the correct forgiving design for cross-version enrichplot churn, not a usability defect.

security.note: No credentials, no raw-string execution, no sensitive-data handling; operates entirely on already-computed in-memory R objects from sibling Skills.

maintainability.note: Clean 3-way separation (SKILL.md concept/reference, usage-guide.md prompts, examples/ runnable scripts); both example scripts verified to run unmodified end-to-end, which is a strong, unusual-for-this-corpus testability signal.

agent_specific.note: Precise trigger scope with explicit hand-offs to sibling Skills for out-of-scope requests (statistics -> go-enrichment/gsea, generic ggplot grammar -> ggplot2-fundamentals). One point held back on Escape Hatches: the Skill never explicitly tells the agent what to do when zero terms/sets survive filtering (clusterProfiler itself degrades gracefully, but the Skill gives no guidance for that case, unlike its shipped GSEA example which does handle it defensively).

key_strengths: Both shipped example scripts (visualization_ora.R, visualization_gsea.R) ran end-to-end unmodified against real clusterProfiler/enrichplot/org.Hs.eg.db -- a reliability signal rare in this corpus.

The Skill's central claims are not just asserted but independently verifiable: the redundancy count (203 raw -> 77 simplified), the no-barplot-for-gseaResult design decision, and GeneRatio != FoldEnrichment were all confirmed by real execution against real package internals.

Common Errors and Per-Method Failure Modes sections correctly anticipate and pre-empt most real failure modes an agent will actually hit (missing termsim slot, deprecated cnetplot args, GeneRatio misread as effect size).
Clean progressive disclosure: SKILL.md carries the conceptual/reference load, usage-guide.md carries prompts and quick reference, examples/ carries the two runnable scripts -- each file does one job.

recommendations.title: upsetplot()'s ggupset dependency is undocumented
recommendations.problem: upsetplot() fails with 'The package "ggupset" is required' on a stock install, but unlike ridgeplot/goplot (whose ggridges/ggarchery Suggests-only dependencies ARE listed), ggupset is never mentioned in SKILL.md or usage-guide.md.
recommendations.root_cause: The Prerequisites section in usage-guide.md was written before or without checking upsetplot()'s own Suggests requirement.
recommendations.fix: Add ggupset to usage-guide.md's Prerequisites install line and to SKILL.md's Common Errors table, matching the existing ggridges/ggarchery pattern exactly.

recommendations.title: treeplot() on a compareClusterResult crashes under the current enrichplot/ggplot2 combination
recommendations.problem: treeplot(pairwise_termsim(compareClusterResult), nCluster=5) throws a ggplot2 aesthetics-length error, reproducible with both the documented 'nCluster' argument and its suggested replacement 'cluster.params=list(n=5)'. SKILL.md's Version Compatibility note calls out cnetplot/emapplot/goplot argument churn but not this crash.
recommendations.root_cause: The Skill's Tool Taxonomy table lists treeplot as supporting 'ORA + GSEA' without a per-class caveat, and its own worked treeplot example only exercises a plain enrichResult, so the compareClusterResult path was never verified against the installed package combination.
recommendations.fix: Either verify and fix the compareClusterResult + treeplot path against a current enrichplot release, or add an explicit caveat in the Decision Tree / Common Errors table that treeplot on a compareClusterResult should be verified with a minimal example before use, with emapplot offered as the working alternative for that class (already confirmed working in this audit).

recommendations.title: No explicit guidance for zero-surviving-terms/sets
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md never tells the agent what to do when enrichGO/gseGO returns zero significant rows, even though the Skill's own shipped GSEA example defensively handles exactly this case in its own code.
recommendations.root_cause: The defensive pattern lives only in examples/visualization_gsea.R's if (nrow(...) > 0) branch, not called out as a general rule in SKILL.md's Escape Hatches or Common Errors.
recommendations.fix: Add one line to the Common Errors table: 'zero significant terms/sets -> report the count and stop, do not attempt to plot an empty object' (mirroring what the shipped example already does).

recommendations.title: Deprecated 'nCluster' argument used in the Skill's own primary treeplot example
recommendations.problem: The installed enrichplot (1.26.6) already warns 'Use cluster.params = list(n = your_value) instead of nCluster. The nCluster parameter will be removed in the next version', but SKILL.md's own code examples use nCluster= throughout.
recommendations.root_cause: SKILL.md was written against an enrichplot version where nCluster was still the primary (non-deprecated) argument name.
recommendations.fix: Switch the Skill's treeplot() examples to cluster.params=list(n=5) and mention the rename in the Version Compatibility note alongside the cnetplot/emapplot/goplot churn it already documents.
